source_refs.note: 13. Nitroalkanes (CₙH₂ₙ₊₁NO₂) (–C–NO₂): a main subheading of 19.4 Nomenclature of Aliphatic Organic Compounds, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 41-45.

blocks.prompt:
a) What are the systematic names of the following?
i) (CH₃)₃COH
ii) CH₃CCl₃
iii) CH₂=CH–CH₂–OH
iv) CH₃COC₆H₅
v) CH₂ = C(CH₃)COOCH₃
blocks.explanation:
i) 2-methylpropan-2-ol
ii) 1,1,1-trichloroethane
iii) prop-2-en-1-ol
iv) 1-phenylethanone (phenylethanone)
v) methyl 2-methylpropenoate (methyl 2-methylprop-2-enoate)

blocks.prompt:
b) Draw the structures of the following.
i) 2 - methylbutanal
ii) prop -2- ylmethanoate
iii) phenylethanoic acid
iv) cyclohexanone
v) 3 - methylpentanal
blocks.explanation:
i) CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CHO
ii) HCOOCH(CH₃)₂ (propan-2-yl methanoate)
iii) C₆H₅CH₂COOH
iv) a six-carbon ring with =O on one carbon (C₆H₁₀O)
v) CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CHO

answer_figure.alt: Five structural formulas: (i) 2-methylbutanal CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CHO; (ii) propan-2-yl methanoate H-C(=O)-O-CH(CH3)-CH3; (iii) phenylethanoic acid, benzene ring-CH2-C(=O)-O-H; (iv) cyclohexanone, a six-cornered ring with =O at one corner; (v) 3-methylpentanal CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CHO.
answer_figure.caption: Answer diagram: structural formulas of 2-methylbutanal, propan-2-yl methanoate, phenylethanoic acid, cyclohexanone and 3-methylpentanal.
answer_figure.long_description: Each structure has its name below it. The aldehydes (i, v) have C=O at the end of the chain with H on that carbon. In the ester (ii) the methanoate part is H–C(=O)–O–, and the propan-2-yl group, CH(CH₃)–CH₃, is joined to the O. In phenylethanoic acid (iii) a CH₂ and then a –COOH group are joined to the benzene ring. Cyclohexanone (iv) is a six-carbon ring with =O on one carbon. Every corner of the rings is a carbon carrying the H atoms it needs.
